subject.title: fix(gateway): require shared secret for tailscale serve auth

question: Should OpenClaw permanently support an opt-in Gateway policy that requires verified Tailscale Serve identity plus token/password authentication and rotates session generation when that policy changes?
rationale: This introduces a new persistent security policy and defines how shared secrets, Tailscale identity, device tokens, hot reload, and active-session invalidation compose; tests can verify implementation but cannot choose that product security contract.

options.title: Adopt layered authentication
options.body: Approve the opt-in contract after current-head Gateway proof and explicit confirmation of device-token reconnect semantics.

options.title: Use existing shared-secret mode
options.body: Decline the new setting and direct operators to disable allowTailscale when they want token/password authentication without retaining Tailscale identity as a second factor.

recommendation.title: Adopt layered authentication
recommendation.body: Approve the opt-in contract after current-head Gateway proof and explicit confirmation of device-token reconnect semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most clearly connects this person to the documented Tailscale product boundary and repository-level direction.
